answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit bids; a public beacon assigns work unpredictably, and a cipher-bound commit reveals the bid only after assignment, limiting cheap copying and targeted collusion. Repeated identities still need separate capital, while provable double-signing or fraud destroys stake. An attacker can wander across names, but cannot multiply influence without tying up real resources and risking their loss.
